findings.current_code:
def cancel_download(self, username: str, transfer_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """DELETE /api/v0/transfers/downloads/{username}/{id} to cancel a transfer."""
    encoded_username = quote(username, safe="")
    encoded_transfer_id = quote(transfer_id, safe="")
    path = f"{_TRANSFERS_DOWNLOAD_ROOT}/{encoded_username}/{encoded_transfer_id}"
    result = self._request_json("DELETE", path, success_statuses={200, 202, 204})
    return result if isinstance(result, dict) else {}
findings.problem: cancel_download adds a DELETE capability to SlskdTransferClient that issues a cancel for any username/transfer_id it is given, with no ownership or state check at this layer. The project's own 22-03-PLAN.md documents that the authenticated endpoint and ownership/state validation (reject non-active/non-owned acquisition rows) are implemented in a separate task (web/job_actions.py, web/api.py) that is not part of this diff, so the caller side that must enforce authorization is unverified from this change alone.
findings.title: New DELETE cancel capability — caller-side authz/ownership check not in view
findings.why_it_matters: If the upstream endpoint ever calls this with user-influenced username/transfer_id without first checking that the authenticated caller owns the corresponding acquisition row, it would allow one user to cancel another user's or another slskd user's in-flight transfer (IDOR). This is a note about an unverified boundary, not a demonstrated bypass, since the enforcing code lives outside this diff.
